text: The dot products between queries and keys grow in magnitude as the dimension d_k increases, which can push the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients [4]. By dividing by √d_k, the model avoids the gradient‑vanishing problem and improves training stability [2][4].

answer:

This scaling is applied directly in the Scaled Dot‑Product Attention formula Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax((QKᵀ)/√d_k)V [3]. By dividing by √d_k, the model avoids the gradient‑vanishing problem and improves training stability [2][4].

answer:

By distilling semantic information into a plain vector quantizer and running a separate 7‑level RVQ in parallel, Mimi can keep semantic tokens distinct while preserving acoustic quality[1].

text:
The hierarchical model in 2507.07955 places an RMSNorm (Zhang & Sennrich 2019) at the end of each network component (E^s, D^s, M) to normalize the final output of every stage [1]. It also adds normalization layers after each residual block to restore balance between processed features and residual information [4].  

In the Transformer described in 1706.03762, every sub‑layer (both in the encoder and decoder) is followed by a layer‑normalization step, i.e., LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)) [5], and the decoder similarly applies layer normalization after each of its three sub‑layers [3].  

The model in 2410.00037 uses RMS normalization (RMSNorm) at the input of the attention blocks, the feed‑forward blocks, and the output linear layer of the Transformer [7].

answer:
The hierarchical model in 2507.07955 places an RMSNorm (Zhang & Sennrich 2019) at the end of each network component (E^s, D^s, M) to normalize the final output of every stage [1]. It also adds normalization layers after each residual block to restore balance between processed features and residual information [4].  

In the Transformer described in 1706.03762, every sub‑layer (both in the encoder and decoder) is followed by a layer‑normalization step, i.e., LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)) [5], and the decoder similarly applies layer normalization after each of its three sub‑layers [3].  

The model in 2410.00037 uses RMS normalization (RMSNorm) at the input of the attention blocks, the feed‑forward blocks, and the output linear layer of the Transformer [7].

text: The chunking router outputs a confidence value p^s ∈[0,1] for each token, indicating how likely the token should be passed into the main stage and thus where a chunk boundary should be placed [2]. During training, a differentiable smoothing module uses this confidence to keep discrete boundaries when p^s ≈ 1.0 and to blend neighboring chunks when p^s ≈ 0.5, creating an adaptive error‑correction mechanism [5]. At inference time, H‑Net dynamically draws boundaries based on these learned confidences, often aligning them with natural delimiters such as whitespace characters [8]. Consequently, the model decides splits by evaluating per‑token confidence and adjusting boundaries through the smoothing module. This process allows H‑Net to allocate compute adaptively across tokens [1].
